narrative_prose: Ryn stood by the thirty-gallon steam-jacketed kettle, the oppressive radiant heat pressing against the harsh structural cold filtering down from the ridge. She watched the copper surface glow a deep umber, masking the lingering scent of roasted myco-protein with the sharp sting of salt-vinegar polish. The low simmer of the heavy stockpots formed a rhythmic baseline against the erratic, distant screech of magnetohydrodynamic Kelvin-Helmholtz shear across the ferrofluid sea. She braced her hands against the counter, preparing to DEFEND the delicate iron-wheat starter crock from the barometric tremors threatening to shake it off the shelf. Realizing the thermal shear was worsening, she threw a handful of salt into the hearth to ATTRACT Silas's attention, knowing he was already calculating the structural load. She quickly moved to CONCEAL the remaining spice reserves beneath the reinforced butcher block before they could be rattled loose. "The shear is throwing off my caramelization curves by three degrees, Engineer," she barked, wiping her brow. She firmly pressed the brass tally-baton into Silas's awaiting hand.
